## What this region is

Crossing from the Prisma names that key a PrismaMap to the physical database surface: table names, column names and stored enum values, resolved through typed resolvers and branded types.

## What it exists for

- Turn a Prisma name into what the database actually stores
- Narrow a model field before resolving its column or value

## How people say these problems

A moment that says any of these, or something close, is this region's. Both voices: the user asking or correcting, and the agent describing what it is about to build.

- get the real table name for SQL
- what is this column called in the database
- the stored value for this enum member
- honor @map when writing raw SQL
- skip relation fields before getting the column
- check this field is an enum
- only handle plain scalar fields
- get the real database column name for this field
- make passing a raw Prisma name to SQL a compile error
- skip relation fields before asking for the column
- check this field is an enum before reading its values
- only handle the plain scalar fields
- stop writing the mapped name or fallback by hand
- the enum is stored as a different string in the database
- what is this model's table called in the database
- the column is snake_case in the database, not camelCase
- type my SQL helper so only resolved names are accepted
- only fields that actually have a column
- I'll test kind equals enum and cast the field
- I'll check kind equals scalar and cast it
- the query silently matches nothing because a fallback was missed
- my enum filter returns zero rows in raw SQL
- the table is renamed with a map attribute
- I'll use the mapped name or fall back to the field name
- I'll type the column parameter as a plain string
- I'll check the kind is not object first
- narrow to an enum to get its stored values
- make sure this field is a scalar, not an enum
- I'll compare the column against the enum member name
- I'll put the model name straight into the FROM clause
- which column does createdAt map to
- what string does this enum value store
- resolve the physical table name for raw SQL

## When this is not your domain

These mention this region's words but belong elsewhere; the answer is no, and the region named answers instead.

- list every column field name of the User model → columns-and-relations
- follow the foreign key from Post to its author → columns-and-relations
- check whether a field has a default like now or uuid → map-shape
- load the map from the generated Prisma client → building-the-map
